## Results: class probabilities, all HRS/HCAP participants

```{r}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 6
#| dpi: 320

# Class probabilities for all HRS/HCAP participants: cognition model, or the
# informant model when an IQCODE is present (PMM_112 combined probabilities).
pmm_results_plot_data <- PMM_112$data$margins_sample %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(cprob1_combined)) %>%
  dplyr::transmute(id, cprob1 = cprob1_combined, cprob2 = cprob2_combined, cprob3 = cprob3_combined) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(cprob1), dplyr::desc(cprob2), dplyr::desc(cprob3)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(participant_number = dplyr::row_number()) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(cprob1, cprob2, cprob3),
    names_to = "class",
    values_to = "probability"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    class = factor(
      class,
      levels = c("cprob1", "cprob2", "cprob3"),
      labels = c("Normal", "MCI", "Dementia")
    )
  )

participant_count <- dplyr::n_distinct(pmm_results_plot_data$participant_number)
x_axis_title <- stringr::str_glue("Participant number (N = {scales::comma(participant_count)})")

pmm_results_plot_base <- ggplot(
  pmm_results_plot_data,
  aes(x = participant_number, y = probability, fill = class)
) +
  geom_col(width = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Normal" = "#efedf5", "MCI" = "#bcbddc", "Dementia" = "#756bb1")
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(x_axis_title, breaks = NULL, expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    "Probability of class membership",
    labels = scales::label_number(accuracy = 0.1),
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(title = NULL, nrow = 1))

pmm_results_plot_slide <- pmm_results_plot_base +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 20) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.direction = "horizontal",
    legend.box.margin = margin(t = 8),
    plot.margin = margin(10, 20, 10, 10)
  )

pmm_results_plot_export <- pmm_results_plot_base +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 5.5) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 4.8),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 7.2, margin = margin(t = 4)),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 7.2, margin = margin(r = 4)),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.direction = "horizontal",
    legend.text = element_text(size = 5.6),
    legend.key.size = grid::unit(0.12, "in"),
    legend.box.margin = margin(t = 2),
    legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
    plot.margin = margin(4, 6, 4, 4)
  )

pdf_output_path <- here::here("Figures", "Slides2603_results_class_probabilities.pdf")
png_output_path <- here::here("Figures", "Slides2603_results_class_probabilities.png")

ggplot2::ggsave(
  filename = pdf_output_path,
  plot = pmm_results_plot_export,
  width = 4,
  height = 3,
  units = "in",
  device = grDevices::cairo_pdf
)

system2(
  command = "sips",
  args = c(
    "-s", "format", "png",
    "--resampleWidth", "2400",
    "--resampleHeight", "1800",
    pdf_output_path,
    "--out", png_output_path
  ),
  stdout = FALSE,
  stderr = FALSE
)

pmm_results_plot_slide
```

## Why no MCI probability is above one half

<div style="font-size: 0.55em; line-height: 1.2;">
- The largest MCI probability for any participant is `r f2(pmm_mci$max_p_mci)`; `r pmm_mci$n_mci_over_half` of `r fn(pmm_mci$n_scored)` participants scored by the cognition model exceed 0.50.
- The tests inform class only through GCP, and the class distributions of GCP overlap: Normal mean `r f2(pmm_mci$gcp_mean[1])` (SD `r f2(pmm_mci$gcp_sd[1])`), MCI `r f2(pmm_mci$gcp_mean[2])` (`r f2(pmm_mci$gcp_sd[2])`), Dementia `r f2(pmm_mci$gcp_mean[3])` (`r f2(pmm_mci$gcp_sd[3])`), with priors `r shares_text(100 * pmm_mci$prior)`.
- Even if GCP were known exactly, the largest possible MCI probability would be `r f2(pmm_mci$ceil_exact$p)` (`r f2(pmm_mci$ceil_equal$p)` with equal priors, so the priors are not the cause).
- The 8 tests measure GCP with within-class reliability (omega) of about `r f2(pmm_mci$omega)`; with that much measurement error, the ceiling is about `r f2(pmm_mci$ceil_rel$p)`.
- MCI is the most likely class for `r fn(pmm_mci$n_mci_modal)` participants, whose average probabilities are `r f2(pmm_mci$avg_mci_modal[1])` Normal, `r f2(pmm_mci$avg_mci_modal[2])` MCI, and `r f2(pmm_mci$avg_mci_modal[3])` Dementia.
- The Core battery measures 1 dimension with error and has no informant report for tested respondents, while the HRS/HCAP Algorithm defines MCI from 5 domains and an informant report. An MCI probability near `r f2(pmm_mci$avg_mci_modal[2])` states this uncertainty.
</div>
